In reality, humans use almost all parts of the brain, but not in the way people often imagine. Many areas of the brain are active at any given time, even when we're resting or performing simple tasks. Brain imaging techniques like functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) have shown that different brain regions are active at different times, and some areas may be more active during rest than others.

The idea that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is likely an exaggeration or misinterpretation of the work of psychologist and neuroscientist Paul MacLean, who suggested in his 1965 book "The Triune Brain" that different parts of the brain have evolved for specific functions.

So, to answer your question, there isn't a specific percentage of the brain that humans use. Instead, different areas of the brain are active at different times, and our brains are capable of incredible adaptability and plasticity.
